alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses at a grocery self-checkout. She holds a bag and points at a screen that says Round up for charity?, with a large green Yes button, a small No thanks, and a wine bottle in the cart. Text at the top reads: Call me crazy, but if I'm scanning, bagging, and weighing my own groceries, I want the employee discount. Instead the screen asked me to round up for charity. A pink box at the bottom reads: I am the charity.

alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. Then: a smiling family of five on a dock by a lake house. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses toasts with red wine at a kitchen table beside a laptop. Text at the top reads: My parents raised three kids, paid off a house, and spent a week at the lake every summer on one income. Text below reads: I have two jobs, a budget app, and a payment plan for my teeth. A purple box at the bottom reads: Somebody explain what happened.

She smirks and points at a tablet with tip buttons for 25%, 30% and 35%. Text at the top reads: I ordered at a counter. I filled my own drink. I carried my own tray. And the iPad still wanted 25%. alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses at a kitchen table, pointing at a laptop that says Assessment 4 of 6, while a younger woman in a hoodie looks tired. A glass of red wine sits on the table. Text at the top reads: I keep hearing nobody wants to work anymore. Okay. Maybe. alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1985: a receptionist hands a card to a younger woman beside a rotary phone. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses grimaces at a phone chat, holding her shoulder, wine on the table. Text at the top reads: In 1985 you called the doctor, a woman named Barb answered, and you were seen Thursday. A red box at the bottom reads: Now I need a portal, a password, and a chatbot named Ava who can fit me in March.

Text at the top reads: My homeowners insurance went up again because of "market conditions." Twenty-two years. Zero claims. A red box at the bottom reads: I'm not the market. A woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses pulls her glasses down, side-eyes a man shouting into a phone held out on speaker, and raises one finger. Other people look annoyed. Text at the top reads: If you put your phone on speaker in a waiting room, everyone within fifty yards gets a vote on the conversation. A teal box at the bottom reads: And I vote you hang up.
